title: Constant module sheaves reflect finite generation on a nonempty topos
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] such that its sheaf topos is not empty, meaning that the initial and terminal sheaves of sets are not isomorphic. Let $B$ be a commutative ring and $M$ a $B$-module. Write $B_{\mathcal C}$ and $\underline M$ for the constant ring sheaf and constant module sheaf, obtained by sheafifying the constant presheaves with identity restriction maps [def-sf-site-constant-module-functor]. Say that $\underline M$ is of finite type if for every object $U$ there is a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ on each member of which finitely many sections generate the restricted $B_{\mathcal C}$-module sheaf (equivalently, there is an epimorphism from a finite sum of copies of the restricted regular module). Then $\underline M$ is of finite type if and only if $M$ is a finitely generated $B$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].
